raw_response:
Aiya, you want to know how I'll manage my 3 mu this year? Let me think out loud.

I've been farming this land for 50 years. My wife and I do most of the work — our kids work in town, they send money sometimes but they don't come back for the farming. 3 mu isn't much, but it feeds us and we sell a bit of the wheat and maize.

**Wheat (planted last October, harvesting this June):**
I planted Jimai 22 again, same as always — my neighbor Old Wang has been using it for years, good yield, doesn't fall over. Before planting I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (那种复合肥, the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 jin), worked it in with the small rotary tiller I hire from the村里 guy. Around the Spring Festival when it greens up, I'll topdress urea — maybe 30 jin per mu, depends on how the wheat looks. If it's yellow I put more, if it looks green enough I save some money. I'll water it 3 times I think — once at green-up, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. Well water is expensive now, the electric meter doesn't lie. If it rains good in spring I skip one. Before harvest I'll pay the combine guy — everyone does this now, my back can't take cutting by hand anymore.

**Maize (planting right after wheat in June):**
Same as every year — no-till, just drill the seed in right after the combine leaves. I don't have a week to till, the rain is coming and I need to get it in. I buy Zhengdan 958 seed, it's what everyone plants here. I put some urea and compound fertilizer down at planting, then top-dress urea again when it's about knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat — if it rains I don't irrigate at all, if it's dry in July-August I'll water once or twice. I spray herbicide once after planting for the weeds. Aphids and borers — I watch, if I see them I spray, if not I don't waste the money.

I don't hire labor. My wife and I manage, and the combine and planter we pay by the mu. Costs add up but it's the same every year, I know what to expect.
